text:
Kai: ran a multi-region latency sweep for llama3-small-int8 across us-east / us-west / eu-west (h100 + a100). quick summary below and a link to the raw charts: https://redwood-internal/bench/2305129876 :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Eva: nice — can you paste the p50/p95 matrix here? want to see routing impact before I write sizing recs.

Kai: sure, pasted quick table (batch=1, seq=128, warmup=200, kv/cache warmed). kernel=fused vs vanilla, edge route = direct vs via edge-proxy.

```
region   gpu   route        kernel    p50(ms)   p95(ms)   tok/s
US-EAST  H100  direct       fused     18        65        1.1k
US-EAST  H100  edge-proxy   fused     28        95        0.9k  # +~30ms tail when proxy hop added
US-EAST  A100  direct       fused     22        80        0.9k
US-WEST  H100  direct       fused     20        70        1.05k
US-WEST  H100  edge-proxy   vanilla   33       120        0.75k  # kernel fallback + proxy = big tail
EU-WEST  H100  direct       fused     26        110       0.85k  # longer hop to model pop
EU-WEST  H100  edge-proxy   fused     44        165       0.6k   # worst-case: combined geo + proxy
EU-WEST  A100  direct       vanilla   38        170       0.55k

notes: int8 quant helps throughput but kernel mismatch causes fallback to slower path => p95 blowups.
```

Omar: saw the same in my run — when the fused kernel isn't available we fall back to slower matmul and p95 doubles in eu-west. suspiciously correlated with proxy path (adds ~1-2 extra TCP hops and causes connection re-est).

Lina: two quick suggestions: 1) enforce kernel preload on nodes in eu-west during rollout (`systemctl restart model-kernel-cache` pre-deploy or add to canary hooks) 2) increase small warmup pool for edge-proxy path to avoid cold-conn spikes. both helped ~20-40ms in our staging run. :+1:

Matt: for Dedicated sizing recs — assume worst-case p95 for SLA calc. if target tail <120ms, we need to limit edge-proxy routing for eu-west or reserve extra H100 capacity (20% headroom). rough calc: current direct p95 H100 eu-west=110ms, to get buffer set reserve to handle 1.25x traffic => add 1 extra H100 per 5k rps.

perf-bot: perf run uploaded: https://redwood-internal/bench/2305129876/results.json (includes raw traces, kernel profiles).

Eva: can you also dump kernel availability per host for that run? I want to map p95 spikes to hosts that failed to load fused kernels.

Kai: yep — attaching host list snippet below (sanitized):

```
hosts_missing_fused = [eu-w-23, eu-w-27, us-w-11]
hosts_kernel_load_errors: 2023-11-12T02:13:45Z -> OOM while JITing fused_matmul on eu-w-27
```

Omar: OOM during kernel JITing explains fallback; maybe precompile at image build or use kernel-shared cache. For now I'll push a quick canary that pins kernel version and disables JIT on vulnerable hosts.

Lina: also worth adding routing policy: prefer direct pop unless request size triggers region fallback. simple policy reduces edge-proxy fraction by ~18% in canary.

Kai: next steps: 1) run targeted eu-west canary with kernel preloads + reduced proxy fraction 2) re-run sweep with longer warmup 500 to confirm p95 consistency 3) update sizing note for Dedicated (include 20% H100 buffer)

Eva: sounds good. I'll draft a short note for product/infra with the graphs and suggested routing/kernels.

Matt: thanks — if you want I can pre-author a commit to the Dedicated sizing calc sheet with the H100 buffer suggestion.

Kai: much appreciated. low-churn plan for today: small canary (5% traffic) with kernel pin + warmup, monitor p95 for next 2 hours, revert if spike >+20%

Eva: ping me on results, will validate before sending to infra. :thinking:

Kai: will do.

(threads usually end here)
